messages:
elaine: Customer reported massive token usage and 401 auth errors after upgrading to py-sdk 1.13. Billing spike started ~09:12 UTC.
elaine: Error pattern looks like: repeated 401 -> client refresh -> repeated request -> billed tokens keep increasing.
sam: ETA of the upgrade? any pinned requirements?
elaine: They upgraded from 1.12.4 -> 1.13.0 yesterday via pip.
elaine: Repro steps customer gave:
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'], timeout_ms=3000)
for _ in range(10):
    r = c.generate("hello")
    print(r.status_code)
```
elaine: Logs show: 401, 200, 401, 200, ... but multiple requests per user action.
mike: Could be a retry change. 1.13 had a signature/param refactor around timeouts/retries.
ingrid: Do we have a known regression where "timeout_ms" got ignored or aliased?
mike: Quick check: in 1.12 Client.__init__ accepted timeout_ms and set socket-level timeouts for the request/stream paths. In 1.13 we renamed to request_timeout and left an optional kwarg mapping, but if users pass timeout_ms as a positional/legacy kwarg it can be swallowed by **kwargs in the internal session wrapper and NOT applied to auth refresh path. That makes short timeouts ineffective and lets the auth refresh loop keep retrying.
sam: So SDK is retrying token refresh indefinitely or with a much shorter backoff, causing duplicated token requests and duplicate billing?
mike: Exactly. The auth refresh path uses the new default retry policy which doesn't respect the legacy "timeout_ms"; instead it retries many times.
elaine: Customer-reported workaround: pin to 1.12.5 and the spike stopped immediately. Confirmed by their billing team.
ingrid: Any temporary server-side mitigations we can do? rate-limit their API key to stop burn?
support-bot: Action created: TICKET-4521 (support) assigned to eng-runtime.
mike: Short-term options to give customer: 1) pin to redwood==1.12.5, 2) set env REDWOOD_DISABLE_AUTO_RETRY=1 (hidden flag) which disables client-side refresh retries, 3) upgrade to 1.13.1 once we publish patch.
sam: Patch timeline?
mike: We have a fix PR that maps legacy timeout_ms into the auth/refresh path and ensures retries respect per-client settings. Targeting 1.13.1 release in 24h after internal QA.
elaine: I've sent the pin instructions and env workaround to the customer. They're pinning to 1.12.5 for now and asking for ETA on the patch.
ingrid: Add regression test to prevent silent kwarg drop for future releases.
mike: Agreed — adding unit + integration test that verifies "timeout_ms" flow through refresh and streaming code paths.
sam: Can we also add a deprecation warning when "timeout_ms" is passed so it doesn't get silently dropped?
mike: Yes, will add a runtime warning in 1.13.1 if legacy kwargs observed.
elaine: Customer replied: thanks, they applied the pin and billing usage dropped. They'll hold on upgrade until 1.13.1.
support-bot: Updated ticket TICKET-4521: customer accepted pin workaround; ENG assigned; priority: high. :white_check_mark:
elaine: Closing loop here — I'll follow up once 1.13.1 is out and confirm the customer upgrades.
